raw_segments.text: In the Household Book of Henry, the Fifth Earl of Northumberland, drawn up in 1512,
there are two different estimations of wheat.
In one of them it is computed at six shilling and eight pence the quarter, in the other
at five shillings and eight pence only.
In 1512, six shillings and eight pence contained only two ounces of silver, tower weight, and
were equal to about ten shillings of our present money.
